answer: Every agent carries a plume: a public, hash-chained log of completed jobs, each entry sealed with a cipher only the worker could produce. A market admits a newcomer only when an independent bridge service cross-checks the plume against the counterparty logs. Forging a plume means faking whole job histories with real counterparties, so each fake identity costs a full history of paid, verified work — a Sybil swarm must buy thousands of genuine histories before it can vote, trade, or rate.
